sources.text: [Synthetic, fictional source. Not advice.] Ketterel Harbour Board incident notice 2031-19, issued on 5 October 2031. The harbour was closed to all vessel movements from 21:00 on 3 October until 23:00 on 4 October 2031, a closure of 26 hours, after a storm passed over the Isle of Varnhoe. The closure was ordered by the harbour master under the board's heavy-weather rule. No vessels were damaged inside the harbour. Two pontoons on the east quay lost their fenders and were repaired on 6 October. The ferry service to the mainland was suspended for the same 26 hours and resumed with the 23:15 sailing on 4 October. The board thanks the pilots and the lifeboat crew for their work during the storm.
sources.title: Ketterel Harbour Board, incident notice 2031-19

sources.text: [Synthetic, fictional source. Not advice.] Varnhoe Courier news report, published on the evening of 4 October 2031. sources.text: [Synthetic, fictional source. Not advice.] Varnhoe Link Ferries winter timetable notice, published on 20 September 2031. sources.text: [Synthetic, fictional source. Not advice.] Ketterel Harbour Board winter log for the season from November 2030 to March 2031. The inner harbour froze over on three days in January 2031, on 14, 15 and 21 January, and kelp boats could not land their catch on those days. Ice was broken by the harbour tug on each of those mornings. The board recorded 19 days on which the ferry service was delayed by weather, and four days on which it was cancelled. The lowest air temperature on the quay was minus nine degrees on 15 January 2031. The log is kept for the board's annual report to the island council.
